title: The March 1989 information-management proposal

body: CERN's historical page on Tim Berners-Lee's proposal says that in March 1989 he submitted a proposal for an information management system to his boss, Mike Sendall. Sendall wrote on it the words "Vague, but exciting." The page records that reaction and the date. It is a CERN account of the proposal's reception, not the full text of the proposal. The system that grew out of the proposal became the World Wide Web: linked documents identified by addresses and fetched over the Internet. The 1989 note is a proposal inside one laboratory for managing information. It is not, at that date, a public network with the later scale of the Web. Treating the marginal comment as a technical specification would misread a manager's note. The technical design is in the proposal itself.
